questions.question: Define Ethnobotany as an Interdisciplinary science.
questions.solution_html:
• Ethnobotany is an interdisciplinary science which combine insights from the following fields
  • Botany-Identification classification of plants.
  • Anthropology- Study of cultural practices and social context.
  • Pharmacology-Validation of medicinal properties.
  • Ecology-Understanding plant-environment relationships.
  • Agriculture-Traditional farming and crop management.
  • Lingustics-study of local plant names.
  • Sociology-analysis of knowledge transmission.
  • Economics- Understanding plant-based livelihoods.
  • Law & IPR-Protection of traditional knowledge and rights.
  • This integration makes ethnobotany a complete science.
questions.final_answer: This integration makes ethnobotany a complete science
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Differentiate between process patent and product patent.
questions.solution_html:
• A product patent protects a final invention, such as a drug or device, regardless of how it was made.
  • Eg A patent on a new chemical compound or a specific medication. A process patent protects the
  • specific method or technique used to create a product, but not the product itself. Eg A patent on the
  • novel method used to synthesize that same chemical compound. Liberal valuation.

questions.question: Write an account of the ethnobotanical practices involving Coscinium fenestratum, Dioscorea, Vitex negundo, and Gloriosa superba.
questions.solution_html:
• Dioscorea, Vitex negundo and Gloriosa superba.
  • Coscinium fenestratum
  • The stem and root are rich in berberine, used in traditional medicine; Used for treating fever
  • diabetes, jaundice, ulcers, and skin diseases; Tribal communities use the yellow dye extracted from
  • the stem for colouring fabrics and for ritualistic purposes; Antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory
  • properties recognized in Ayurveda and Siddha systems.
  • Dioscorea spp
  • Edible tubers are a staple food for many tribal groups during food scarcity; Used for treating
  • rheumatism, constipation, and stomach disorders; Certain species (like D. oppositifolia, D. alata)
  • are rich in diosgenin, a steroidal compound used in modern pharmaceutical industries; Tribal
  • women use some Dioscorea species for contraceptive and menstrual regulation.
  • Vitex negundo
  • Leaves are used as a poultice for joint pain, swelling, and wounds; Smoke from burning leaves is
  • used as a mosquito repellent in rural households; Decoction of leaves used to treat fever, respiratory
  • issues, and menstrual disorders; Considered a sacred plant in some communities and planted near
  • homes.
  • Gloriosa superba
  • Rhizomes and seeds are used in small quantities for treating snake bites, gout, and ulcers; Highly
  • toxic if consumed in large quantities; used carefully by experienced tribal healers; Also used in
  • fertility-related rituals and traditional abortifacient remedies; Contains colchicine, a compound
  • used in modern medicine for treating gout and cancer research.

questions.question: Explain the step by step procedure for obtaining patent.
questions.solution_html:
• Step 1: Filing of Patent Application- To be filed at the appropriate branch of the Patent Office
  • under whose jurisdiction he normally resides. Applicant shall submit the necessary documents
  • while filing the application. The patent applications can also be filed electronically through the
  • website of the patent office (www.ipindia.nic.in). Upon receiving the patent application, Patent
  • Office will issue the patent application number and date of filing, to the applicant.
  • Step 2: Publication-The patent application will be published in the official journal of Patents after
  • the expiry of 18 months from the date of filing or date of priority of the application.
  • Step 3: Opposition-Upon publication of the patent application, any person can file pre grant
  • opposition to the Controller of Patents against the grant of patent.
  • Step 4: Request for Examination/Expedited Examination
  • The applicant or any interested person must file request for examination for getting their patent
  • application examined by the Patent Office. Every patent application will be examined only up on
  • the receipt of such request.
  • Step 5: Issuance of First Examination Report (FER) -The Patent Office will conduct detailed
  • examination on the patent application to check whether the invention possesses the criteria of
  • novelty. inventiveness and industrial application and issues a First Examination Report (FER) to
  • the applicant, which contains the objections raised by the Patent Office.
  • Step 6: Reply to the Examination Report
  • The applicant must give his/her response to the objections and clarifications in the First
  • Examination Report within 6 months from the date of issue of the FER. If the applicant is not able
  • the response within the prescribed time, the application will be abandoned.
  • Step 7: Grant of Patent and issuance of Certificate
  • The applicant meets the objections and clarifications asked for in the FER, the Controller will grant
  • patent and the details of the Patent will be entered in the register of Patents. Patent Certificate will
  • be issued to the applicant within one month from the date of grant of patent
  • Step 8: Renewal fees
  • The duration of the Patent is 20 years from the data of filing of the application. To keep the patent
  • in force, renewal fees should be paid before the expiration of the second year or the succeeding
  • year from the date of fling of patent.
  • Step 9: Post grant opposition
  • Upon grant of patent also, any interested person, based on different grounds, may file a post grant
  • opposition in Form 7 along with prescribed fee to the Controller against the grant
  • of patent, within one year from the date of publication of grant of patent.
questions.final_answer: of patent, within one year from the date of publication of grant of patent

  • application examined by the Patent Office. Every patent application will be examined only up on
  • the receipt of such request.
  • Step 5: Issuance of First Examination Report (FER) -The Patent Office will conduct detailed
  • examination on the patent application to check whether the invention possesses the criteria of
  • novelty. inventiveness and industrial application and issues a First Examination Report (FER) to
  • the applicant, which contains the objections raised by the Patent Office.
  • Step 6: Reply to the Examination Report
  • The applicant must give his/her response to the objections and clarifications in the First
  • Examination Report within 6 months from the date of issue of the FER. If the applicant is not able
  • the response within the prescribed time, the application will be abandoned.
  • Step 7: Grant of Patent and issuance of Certificate
  • The applicant meets the objections and clarifications asked for in the FER, the Controller will grant
  • patent and the details of the Patent will be entered in the register of Patents. Patent Certificate will
  • be issued to the applicant within one month from the date of grant of patent
  • Step 8: Renewal fees
  • The duration of the Patent is 20 years from the data of filing of the application. To keep the patent
  • in force, renewal fees should be paid before the expiration of the second year or the succeeding
  • year from the date of fling of patent.
  • Step 9: Post grant opposition
  • Upon grant of patent also, any interested person, based on different grounds, may file a post grant
  • opposition in Form 7 along with prescribed fee to the Controller against the grant
  • of patent, within one year from the date of publication of grant of patent.
questions.final_answer: of patent, within one year from the date of publication of grant of patent
